requirements.note: Edge-to-edge 3-column grid of 600 HSL squares with centred emoji, newest first; liked tiles carry a heart badge.
Filter button in the nav bar opens a native menu with All Boards plus 10 boards; the title and count update (Coast: 64 tiles).
Pushed detail with a large square, title, board and date; swiping left/right steps through neighbours (n of 600), and there are prev/next buttons too. The nav title is a generic 'Tile'.
Heart in the nav bar plus a Like/Liked button in the detail view; the Liked tab shows liked tiles in the same grid with its own filter and select.
Select puts circles on tiles; nav bar shows 'N selected', Select All, Like, Delete; delete asks for confirmation in an alert. Bulk Like exits select mode.
Likes and deletions (597 tiles, Liked count) survive relaunch.

bugs: After a bulk delete the large title briefly sits 20pt higher than normal (Library at y=103 vs 123) until the next layout.
tells: Grid tiles are exposed to accessibility as Switches ('Switch … value=0'), so VoiceOver reads each photo tile as a toggle.
Selection badges are white rounded squares with a blue check / blue ring, not the system filled-circle checkmark used in Photos.
In select mode the large-title area turns into an empty white band about 60pt tall above the grid.
When the title collapses on scroll, the inline title and the '597 tiles · Newest first' subtitle sit over the scrolling tiles and are hard to read.
Detail view: the symbol stays small in the large tile, and the nav title is a generic 'Tile' instead of the tile's name.
Hearts are plain black, not tinted, in the detail view and grid badges.
Thin, slightly uneven grey gutter lines between tiles.
At the largest text size the subtitle truncates ('Newest fi…'), the select title truncates to '0 selec…', the badges don't scale, and the date wraps onto two lines.
A.scroll: Smooth native momentum scrolling with no blank or popping rows; flings and pull-to-top behave like a UIKit list, and scroll position is kept on returning from a tile.

requirements.note: 3-column grid of rounded HSL squares with centred emoji, newest first, with small gutters; liked tiles show a heart badge in the corner.
'All boards' pill opens a native menu with All plus 10 boards; the count updates (Coast: 64), and the filter bar stays pinned while scrolling.
Detail is a native paged horizontal collection that follows the finger; it shows board, serif title and date, with 'n of 600' in the nav bar and arrow buttons.
Big 'Add to Liked' / 'Liked' button in the detail view; the Liked tab ('Worth keeping.') shows liked tiles in the same grid with a filter.
Select mode shows system checkmark circles and a bottom bar with count, Select all, Like and Delete; delete is confirmed and followed by an Undo snackbar.
Deletions (597) and likes (62 liked) survive relaunch.

bugs: The delete confirmation appears as a popover whose arrow points at the top-middle tile, not at the Delete button that triggered it.
tells: Branded custom header (stack icon + 'THE COLLECTION' small caps, serif 'Moodboard' headline and tagline) replaces a system large title, and the header never collapses into the nav bar.
Cream background and an orange-red accent with serif type: a styled, web/marketing-like look rather than system colours.
The bulk-action bar (Like / Delete capsules) and the Undo snackbar are drawn by hand above the tab bar instead of using a system toolbar.
The unselected Liked tab icon is a filled black heart, which reads as selected.
The detail view has a custom 'Swipe to explore' footer strip with arrows that takes vertical space.
At the largest text size the 'THE COLLECTION' label disappears, leaving only the icon, and the header eats half the screen before the grid.
B.scroll: Smooth native scrolling with a pinned filter bar; no blank rows or stutter on flings, and position is kept on returning from detail (shifts by about 14pt).

why: Both meet every requirement and persist correctly. A looks closer to a stock iOS app, but it has more rough edges: tiles exposed as switches, a blank band in select mode, the collapsed title overlapping the tiles, and truncation at large text. B's custom branding is less system-like but well finished, with a truly paged detail view, system checkmark selection and undo after delete, so it's the one I'd rather ship.
